axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself** — an interface implementation called by MCP clients. It wraps Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) capabilities
as tools: navigation, clicking, screenshots, performance traces, network and console logs.
axes.runtime:
A local process (npx starts stdio, driving the machine's Chrome); GitHub 53,940★, last push 2026-10-21 (API verified) —
one of the top-traffic projects in the MCP ecosystem.
axes.local_files:
What it operates is the browser runtime: pages, network, console; screenshots/traces can be saved to local paths (specified by parameters).
It does not read or write your project source code — that is the filesystem server's job.
axes.background: Lives and dies with the client (a stdio child process); the Chrome instance is launched or attached by it. No background-task semantics.
axes.tools:
Navigation/interaction (click/type/upload), screenshots, performance tracing and analysis, network and console reading,
 emulation (CPU/network throttling), etc.; the complete inventory follows the repo README.
axes.context: No cross-session memory — page state lives in the browser instance; when the session ends the instance closes.
axes.permissions:
**It drives a real browser**: it can visit any URL the client tells it to and interact as the browser.
The official positioning is giving coding agents the ability to "see the browser"; isolation and allowlists rely on client/browser-profile configuration —
there is no official statement of a URL-allowlist mechanism in the server itself.
axes.fit:
Fits: coding agents debugging real pages, performance analysis, the E2E verification loop (change code → look at the browser → change again).
Not a fit: headless bulk scraping (the fetch/firecrawl line); scenarios needing URL-level hard isolation (the server has no such mechanism).

mcp.transport:
**stdio** (npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest); HTTP-mode support status not verified item by item.
Verified against: the repo README (direct-fetched 2026-10-21).
mcp.auth:
No credential layer — it needs no account token; permissions = whatever the browser instance can do.
Support for connecting to an existing Chrome instance (a --connect-to-existing-browser kind of option) not verified item by item.
mcp.scope:
The scope is the browser runtime: arbitrary navigation, interaction, reading network/console, running performance traces.
No official statement of a URL allowlist or approval layer — tightening relies on client-side tool approval and browser-profile isolation.
